messages:
Maya: quick follow-up on the multi-region RFC — need to pick defaults and clarify residency vs latency tradeoffs
Diego: active/active gives best p99 but complicates KV/cache and KMS boundaries
Leah: legal: for region-locked tenants we cannot replicate prompts or any PII outside their region unless explicitly contracted. must be enforced by control plane. :exclamation:
Sam: product asks for a predictable, auditable failover path for enterprise customers. many will accept failover only if they opt in; default should be region-pinned.
Andre: ops-bot ran probes: eu-west1->us-west1 median RTT 170ms, 99p 210ms, packet loss ~0.2% last 72h
Diego: concrete sketch for residency_policy values: [region_locked, opt_in_failover, geo_active] stored on tenant record. routing logic consults this before any LB decision.
Maya: interface boundary: control plane decides routing and returns connection hints. requests carry tenant-id + region_hint header only. runtime should not be making tenancy policy decisions.
Leah: +1. also KMS keys must be scoped per-region for region_locked tenants; keys and encrypted artifacts must not leave region.
Diego: KV cache questions: option A) accept cold-cache on failover (simple); B) warm-replication (async, complex/egress cost); C) selective tag-based replication for keys marked global.
Sam: product leaning: cold-cache acceptable for rare failovers; warm-replication as premium. need UX around cold-start and SLA variation.
Maya: example tenant config proto snippet (informal):
```
TenantRouting:
  tenant_id: "acct_987"
  residency_policy: "region_locked"
  primary_region: "eu-west-1"
  secondary_regions: []
```
Diego: traffic engineering summary: active/active requires global LB (anycast/route53 latency) + affinity and cross-region replication; active/passive can use DNS failover records + health checks (much simpler).
Andre: cost note: cross-region replication and log egress add billable egress — rough estimate +15-25% for tenants opting in to replication. ops needs pricing input.
Leah: compliance addition: audit flag per-tenant that records any cross-region read or failover event; exportable CSV for audits and legal requests.
Maya: consensus proposal:
- Default for residency-sensitive tenants: region_pinned, no cross-region replication, DNS failover if customer explicitly opts-in
- Default for non-sensitive tenants: active/passive (failover) unless they opt into active/active and replication
- Premium: warm-replication for KV/cache to reduce cold-starts
Diego: implementation checklist: control plane: add residency_policy + primary/replicas; infra: region-tagged pools and named endpoints; runtime: keep nodes stateless except local cache and add graceful shutdown flush hooks.
Sam: rollout ask: can we beta with 2-3 enterprise tenants? also need price model for warm-replication and active/active.
Maya: proposed rollout cadence: 1) tenant metadata + DNS failover prototype (3w) 2) audit logs + region KMS scoping (2w) 3) beta with handful of customers (4w) 4) warm-replication as premium (6-8w)
Diego: blockers: infra needs cross-region KMS support and additional RBAC on control plane APIs. I'll open infra ticket after this thread.
Leah: I'll draft compliance checklist for region_locked and opt-in failover flows and post to #legal-compliance by EOD.
Andre: ops will create staging failover runbooks and synthetic drills; will capture metrics and cold-warm cache deltas.
Maya: action items:
- Diego -> infra RBAC/KMS ticket
- Leah -> compliance checklist
- Sam -> pricing proposal for warm-replication + egress assumptions
- Andre -> staging failover playbook + synthetic drills
- Maya -> update RFC with this thread summary and next PR link
Sam: 👍 meeting tomorrow 09:30 PT to lock beta list
Diego: noted, starting infra ticket today
Leah: posting checklist draft shortly
ops-bot: [reminder] Multi-region rollout sync 2025-11-21 16:30 UTC
Maya: thanks all :heart:
